prompt: What breed of dog is the "Doge" meme?
funFact: The real dog, Kabosu, was a rescue from a Japanese puppy mill.

prompt: What does "LOL" stand for?
funFact: Countless parents have signed condolence texts "LOL" thinking it meant lots of love.

prompt: What does "BRB" mean online?
funFact: It survived from chat rooms where leaving without warning read as walking out mid-sentence.

prompt: What is a "selfie"?
funFact: The word first appeared in an Australian online forum, in a post apologising for a blurry photo.

prompt: What does adding a hashtag to a post do?
funFact: No platform designed it — a user suggested borrowing the symbol from chat channels.

prompt: What does "DM" stand for?
funFact: Sliding into them is a phrase barely a decade old, and it already sounds dated.

prompt: What is an emoji?
funFact: The name is Japanese for "picture character" and has nothing to do with the word emotion.

prompt: What does it mean for a post to "go viral"?
funFact: The metaphor is literal enough that epidemiologists study both with the same equations.

prompt: What does "IRL" stand for?
funFact: The phrase implies the other place is not real, which fewer people would now agree with.

prompt: What is a "thread" on social media?
funFact: The word came from 1980s message boards, where replies were literally strung together.

prompt: The "Distracted Boyfriend" meme is originally what?
funFact: The same models appear in dozens of stock photos, forming an accidental cinematic universe.

prompt: Which platform's logo was a bird until 2023?
funFact: The bird's official name was Larry, after basketball legend Larry Bird.

prompt: Which platform is built around short vertical videos?
funFact: It grew out of a lip-syncing app that was folded into it, taking its users along.

prompt: Which platform is built around live game streaming?
funFact: It began as a spin-off of a site where one man broadcast his entire life from a head camera.

prompt: A "Rickroll" sends you to a song by whom?
funFact: He has said he finds it funny, and re-recorded the song decades later to lean into it.

prompt: Which platform popularised the "story" that disappears?
funFact: Every large rival copied the format within four years, mostly without changing the name.

prompt: Which file format is used for short looping animations?
funFact: It was designed in 1987 for slow modems, and outlived every format meant to replace it.

prompt: Which site is built around pinning images to boards?
funFact: It ran invite-only for its first two years, which is unusual for something that visual.

prompt: "Doomscrolling" means reading what, endlessly?
funFact: The word spread in 2020, but the behaviour it names is as old as the rolling news ticker.

prompt: Which chat app is organised into servers and voice channels?
funFact: It was built for gamers who needed to talk while playing, then everyone else moved in.

prompt: What was the first YouTube video about?
funFact: "Me at the zoo" (2005) is 19 seconds long and still up.

prompt: Who coined the word "meme" in 1976?
funFact: He meant it as the cultural equivalent of a gene — cat pictures came later.

prompt: In which year did YouTube launch?
funFact: It was bought by Google within twenty months, before it had made any money at all.

prompt: The "This is fine" dog comes from which webcomic?
funFact: In the full strip the dog melts — the calm two panels everyone shares are only the setup.

prompt: The Nyan Cat had a body made of what?
funFact: The animation and the song were made by two different people who had never worked together.

prompt: In which year did Instagram launch?
funFact: It started as a check-in app with photos bolted on, and everything else was stripped out.

prompt: The "Harlem Shake" videos used a track by which producer?
funFact: The dance in the videos is not the Harlem Shake, and dancers from Harlem said so loudly.

prompt: "Charlie bit my finger" was uploaded to share with…
funFact: It was set to public only because the family could not work out how to send a large file.

prompt: Grumpy Cat's expression was caused by…
funFact: Her owners insisted she was friendly; the face was simply the face she had.

prompt: In which year did Wikipedia launch?
funFact: It began as a side project to feed a slower encyclopaedia written only by experts.

prompt: As of 2020, the most-retweeted post ever was…
funFact: Yusaku Maezawa offered ¥100m to random retweeters — 4+ million obliged.

prompt: Keyboard Cat's original footage was recorded in which decade?
funFact: Charlie Schmidt filmed his cat Fatso in 1984; the internet found it 23 years later.

prompt: The "Success Kid" photo was taken where?
funFact: He is not celebrating anything — he is about to eat a handful of sand.

prompt: What is the name of Reddit's mascot?
funFact: The name is a pun on "what's new", which is roughly what the whole site is for.

prompt: The "Dancing Baby" animation spread in which decade?
funFact: It was a sample file bundled with 3D software, forwarded by email until it reached television.

prompt: What was YouTube originally built to be?
funFact: Nobody uploaded any dating videos, so the founders opened it to whatever people had.

prompt: The hashtag was first proposed by a user of which platform?
funFact: The company initially thought it looked too technical for ordinary people to bother with.

prompt: The first photograph put on the web showed…
funFact: They were a group of physicists at CERN, and the web was barely a year old at the time.

prompt: The "Numa Numa" video used a song by which band?
funFact: The song is Romanian, and the man in the video was filming himself in his bedroom.

prompt: What was Twitter originally called?
funFact: Vowels were dropped to fit a five-character text short code, the way other services did then.
